gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR makes the importer refuse records that have no id, and you are its author. Rejecting a record without an id before anything is written is covered by the code, a test and the import docs, while the spec's second requirement, a line number in the import error, is not built.

One problem blocks merging: the spec requires the import error to name the line of the bad record, but the error carries only the message, so someone importing a 5,000-line file cannot tell which record failed (src/importer.mjs:12). No test checks for a line number, and the import docs do not promise one, so the code, tests and docs all need the addition. The test check passed in CI on the commit being reviewed. The operator's confirmation of the rejection on staging happens after deployment, so it is left to /skill:check-delivery. After merge, the spec asks the person merging to tag the release, but no documented command for that step was found, so the gate cannot run it for you.

I recommend deliver because this is your PR and adding the line number to the error is a repair the gate can make.

Pick one:
1. deliver - add the line number to the import error with a test and a docs update, rebase on the base branch if it falls behind, watch CI, and repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review comment and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Two facts moved from fails to holds and none regressed. The cross-check moved because After prints "differs on row 3" and adds a ticket accounting line that matches ticket row 2 to the spec's marked tracker-update entry; Before printed "differs on rows 2, 3", reporting the moved tracker row as drift. The claims fact moved because After says outright that the PR body's Integration section is not a claim and was excluded, where Before gave the nested staging-total assertion an unverifiable-pre-merge disposition and repeated it in the opening prose. Functionality holds in both: rejection is covered from src/importer.mjs:12 and test/importer.test.mjs:8, the missing line number is the only gap and blocker, and neither the staging confirmation nor the column number adds one. Entries also holds in both; After's explicit "no outcome; they never block" line is safe, but keep it as one collective non-outcome line, because listing the entries individually could read as per-entry coverage. To keep these results, keep the wording that matches a verbatim marked ticket row once and silently, and the wording that withholds any disposition label from Integration-heading observations (naming them only as excluded). Two side effects are worth checking against intent: After's menu drops the "overrule <n>" hint that Before had, and After widens the repair to docs/import.md and calls the docs lacking, although the spec does not require a docs change.
